definition: Provide a simplified, higher level interface that delegates to a set of subsystem interfaces, making the subsystem easier to use for clients.
ruleOfThumb: When many clients must interact with several complex subsystems, introduce a single coordinating interface that simplifies common tasks.

citation.author: Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides
citation.bookTitle: Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software

questions.prompt: Given the ApiGateway class below, which description best matches its role in this module?

options.text: It provides a simplified high level interface to multiple complex subsystem classes used throughout this module.
options.explanation: This class hides the direct interactions with SubsystemA and SubsystemB behind a single API for callers. In design-pattern terms the gateway consolidates common subsystem operations into one entry point so callers are decoupled from subsystem interfaces and sequencing.

options.text: It enforces transactional consistency by coordinating distributed operations across subsystems and managing rollback on failure.
options.explanation: This is a plausible misread because coordination looks transactional, but the snippet shows simple delegation without rollback, compensation, or transaction boundaries. Introducing a transaction coordinator is a different responsibility than providing a simplified interface.

options.text: It acts as a dependency injection container that resolves and injects subsystem instances into clients at runtime automatically.
options.explanation: This choice confuses object creation and DI responsibilities with a wrapper API. The shown class invokes subsystems directly for an operation rather than performing resolution, lifecycle management, or configurable injections.

options.text: It is a factory responsible for creating and configuring subsystem objects based on client requested types and options.
options.explanation: A factory focuses on object creation and configuration. The snippet demonstrates behavioral orchestration of multiple subsystems for a client call, not returning configured subsystem instances for later use.

questions.prompt: Why introduce a single gateway class in this application service instead of leaving calls spread across callers?

options.text: It provides a simpler unified interface that hides multiple subsystem details from client code.
options.explanation: A single gateway reduces the surface area exposed to clients and hides subsystem APIs and sequencing. That simplification is the primary motivation for a high level wrapper here.

options.text: It centralizes transaction and rollback concerns so distributed subsystem operations can be coordinated from a single place.
options.explanation: Centralized transaction management is a valid concern when operations must be atomic, but the gateway pattern focuses on simplifying the API surface. Transaction coordination may require additional infrastructure beyond a simple gateway.

options.text: It consolidates object creation so tests can substitute mocks more easily without changing multiple construction sites.
options.explanation: Consolidating construction can improve testability, yet that is a side benefit. The shown gateway primarily unifies behavior rather than acting as a creation factory or test seam provider.

options.text: It adapts differing external protocols into one internal interface so the system tolerates multiple client protocols.
options.explanation: Adapting external protocols is the responsibility of an adapter or translator. While a gateway can perform adaptation, the core intent illustrated is API simplification across subsystems rather than protocol translation.

questions.prompt: Which version better improves client code maintainability and why? Review both implementations and choose one.

options.text: Version A keeps orchestration in the controller and avoids introducing an extra wrapper class that hides details.
options.explanation: Keeping orchestration in the controller may seem simpler initially, but it spreads sequencing logic across callers, increasing coupling to subsystem APIs and making future changes harder. Adding a single gateway centralizes orchestration and reduces duplication across controllers.

options.text: Version B centralizes subsystem orchestration behind one higher level interface across the module boundary.
options.explanation: Version B extracts sequencing and subsystem interactions into one reusable entry point, which reduces coupling, keeps controllers thin, and localizes change. This aligns with the intent of a facade style abstraction to simplify client-side usage and maintenance. See Gamma et al. and refactoring literature for guidance on reducing surface area and centralizing orchestration.
